findings.where: §5.2 F1 item 7; §5.4 tests/lib.js addWin (:350) and boardUp (:489); settings.js:1593-1645 (the code it ports)
findings.problem: Item 7 can't work as written. (1) §5.4 makes addWin wait up to 2 s for document.fonts.ready in the new frame. With every .woff2 held about 3 s, the first addWin waits its full 2 s, so by the second or third window Inter has already arrived. That breaks 'open the widgets before it arrives', and the run is timing-bound and flaky. Only boardUp gets { fonts: false }. (2) The ported checks need their listeners in place before the font lands: window.__drawn and __fontsIn for Task Timer's pie, and Board21.on('resize') with loadingdone for the resize. Today's test installs them, then triggers the font by choosing a text style (settings.js:1596-1599, :1636-1639). After this release a frame starts loading Inter as soon as the SDK runs, so listeners added after the frame opens can miss it. (3) Holding fonts on a 3 s timer with fixed waits is the flaky part. Today's 0.7 s hold worked because the test itself chose when the font was asked for.
findings.fix: In §5.2 item 7, replace "with every `.woff2` held back about 3 s, open the widgets before it arrives (with `boardUp(page, { fonts: false })`, so the helper doesn't wait for it)" with: "hold every `.woff2` request behind a gate the test opens (`ctx.route(/\.woff2$/, async r => { await gate; await r.continue(); })`, no timer). Record draws and font arrival in every frame from the start with `ctx.addInitScript` (wrap `CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.fillText` into `window.__drawn`, note `loadingdone` times, and listen for the window's `resize`). Open the board with `boardUp(page, { fonts: false })` and each widget with `addWin(page, id, { fonts: false })`. Then open the gate." In §5.4's lib.js row, add: "`addWin(p, id, { fonts: false })` skips the frame's wait too."

findings.problem: F1 item 2 checks only `->`. In Inter 4.001, `<-` is made into ← by another route: calt lookup 48, a chaining lookup with input [less][hyphen], calls ligature lookups 49 (less+hyphen → arrowleft) and 50 (.case). The recipe's search only finds ligature lookups listed directly in calt (47 and 51), so 48 stays and the built font still turns `<-` into an arrow. The decision says arrow ligatures are dropped. I found this by reading the source TTF's GSUB with fontTools. Lookup 52 calls only 53, case forms, so it is not an arrow.
findings.fix: In §3.1 step 4 write: "Drop the calt lookups that make `*rrow*` or `uni27F*` glyphs, directly or through the lookups they call (47, 48, and 51 in 4.001; 49 and 50 are called only by 48). Assert exactly 3 are dropped." In §5.2 F1 item 2 write: "`->`, `<-`, and `=>` in spans at 48 px, each plain and with `font-feature-settings: \"calt\" 0`, give the same pictures."

findings.problem: (1) The source it names, r-inter/det/woff2-cmap.js, doesn't exist in this session's files. plans/inter has no det/ folder, and nothing named woff2-cmap.js exists under the scratchpad or /home/user. The builder writes it from scratch. (2) As described it can't read hmtx. Advances need hhea.numberOfHMetrics and maxp.numGlyphs, so those two tables must be parsed too. (3) In WOFF2, glyf and loca are transformed when their transform version is 0, and every other table is transformed when its version is nonzero. A helper that gets this backwards reads every later table at the wrong offset. fontTools 4.68 transforms only glyf and loca by default (woff2TransformedTableTags = ('glyf','loca')), so hmtx is untransformed in our build. A later build could transform it.
findings.fix: Replace the helper's description with: "New helper `tests/woff2.js` (about 70 lines, written from the WOFF2 spec): reads the table directory (flags byte, tag index or 4-byte tag, UIntBase128 origLength, and transformLength only when the table is transformed: glyf or loca with transform version 0, any other table with version 1-3), runs `zlib.brotliDecompressSync` on the one stream, and slices tables in directory order. It returns `cmap` (formats 4 and 12), `fvar` axes, `avar` segment maps, and advances from `hmtx`, read with `hhea.numberOfHMetrics` and `maxp.numGlyphs`. It throws if `hmtx` is transformed. The build keeps fontTools' default, which transforms only glyf and loca."
